narrative.overview: PasteTrace reads as a precision laboratory instrument meets a factory HMI terminal: a dark control surface by default (with a light mode of the same identity), muted steel-blue accents, monospace data, and hairline separators. The density is deliberately high (a cockpit, not an airy gallery) because the visitor is an engineer scanning data under time pressure. Every element carries the language of instrumentation: sharp corners, thin borders, tabular numerals, and status conveyed through disciplined semantic color rather than decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Two modes of one identity: Steel Blue dark (default) and Steel Blue light, toggled once for the whole console.
One accent (steel blue) for brand and interactive controls; amber/red/green reserved for semantic status; a separate data-viz ramp for charts.
Monospace for numerals, labels, IDs, and technical values; sans-serif for body and section titles.
Flat, hairline-separated surfaces; no decorative shadows or neon glows; sharp 2-4px corners.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: One accent (steel blue) carries brand and interaction. Amber, red, and green exist only as semantic status; blue only as the user-chat tint. Any new color must earn a semantic role before it may appear.

rules.name: The Role Separation Rule
rules.body: A long, high-scoring cause bar is not 'good': charts use the data-viz ramp, never the status-good or brand tokens.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: All numeric readouts set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so values align in columns and feel like instrument readouts.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat and separated by tone and hairline borders. Hover, active, and selected states are communicated with border color, text color, and low-opacity tints; colored side-borders, ambient glows, and drop shadows are not part of the language.

dos: Do keep a single accent for brand and interactive; use status hues only for status and the data-viz ramp for charts.
Do set every numeric readout in mono with tabular-nums.
Do animate bars and reveals with transform/opacity only (scaleX), and honor prefers-reduced-motion.
Do show visible :focus-visible rings on all interactive controls.
Do keep the flat, tonal, hairline-separated surface model; separation comes from tone and borders.
Do keep text and borders inside the documented tokens and scales.
donts: Don't add a second accent, neon glows, gradients, or decorative drop shadows.
Don't animate width/height (layout thrash); use transform.
Don't use thick colored side-borders on cards or bubbles; use tinted backgrounds and full hairlines instead.
Don't switch themes between sections; light and dark are two modes of the same Steel Blue system, toggled once for the whole console via the topbar control.
Don't hide focus outlines, ship pill-shaped containers for standard cards, or use em-dashes in visible copy.
Don't use mono for section titles or body prose.
